Love Me uses Auracast broadcasts both for accessibility and the sound design. | Photo: Curtis Brown

Up a few concrete steps and through the front door of a 200-year-old row house in New York City, I follow a crowd of people into the 178-seat SoHo Playhouse. As we filter to our seats, ushers hand each person a black drawstring bag with a pair of wired headphones connected to a small Auracast receiver. Then, soon after the play begins, we're instructed to put them on.

The headphones are an integral storytelling tool of Love Me - a one-man show from the minds of stand-up comedian and former Saturday Night Live writer Drew Michael and director Prashanth Venkataramanujam. It's a show about love and the bid for connection, told in five chapters …

Read the full story at The Verge.
